football_evidence.question: Can Ohio contain Eastern Michigan’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Ohio, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.1 of the 4.7 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Ohio has the ball (third down): Ohio’s offense converts 54.1% of its third downs, and Eastern Michigan’s defense allows opponents to convert 43.1% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).
When Ohio has the ball (the red zone): Ohio’s offense succeeds on 54.0% of its red-zone plays, and Eastern Michigan’s defense allows success on 52.6% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When Eastern Michigan has the ball (big plays on the ground): Eastern Michigan’s offense turns 3.5% of its runs into explosive gains, and Ohio’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Ohio has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Ohio’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 10.0% of its runs, and Eastern Michigan’s defense stops 18.1% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
contradicting: When Ohio has the ball (big plays through the air): Ohio’s offense turns 6.5% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Eastern Michigan’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.1% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).
In his last two games (Kent State and Sacramento State), Vezza averaged 3.4 yards per attempt, against 7.8 in his four games before that.

When Ohio has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Ohio’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.0% of its dropbacks, and Eastern Michigan’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Ohio has the ball (big plays on the ground): Ohio’s offense turns 7.2% of its runs into explosive gains, and Eastern Michigan’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
quarterbacks: Nick Poulos has completed 38 of 69 passes (55.1%) for 503 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and no interceptions in four games for Ohio, and has been sacked on 5 of 74 dropbacks.
Matt Vezza has completed 41 of 64 passes (64.1%) for 444 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for Ohio, and has been sacked on 6 of 70 dropbacks.

Noah Kim has completed 168 of 284 passes (59.2%) for 1,692 yards, 6.0 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in eight games for Eastern Michigan, and has been sacked on 9 of 293 dropbacks.
